subject: Bayesian models for multiple outcomes nested in domains

messages.author: f9c6a2087c744460
messages.subject: Bayesian models for multiple outcomes nested in domains
parts:
Hi all,

Not a spatial problem this, but I was wondering if models such as those described by Thurston et al (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3031784/) for multiple outcomes nested within domains can be implemented in INLA.
I am trying to learn about these models and implementations in jags that i'm playing with seem to be spectacularly slow. I haven't seen any reference to INLA modelling multiple outcomes, but I thought it was worth asking. 

Many thanks,
James

messages.author: f9c6a2087c744460
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Bayesian models for multiple outcomes nested in domains
parts:
Hi,

So I can't share my own data, and cannot find suitable open data, so I've had a go at simulating typical data for anyone who thinks they might be able to implement these models - R script attached (its crude, but it approximates the kind of data I'm trying to analyse). What I want to do is model multiple outcomes in a hierarchical structure by domain (this kind of problem comes up in psychometric data, EEG data and probably other areas). The theory is here: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3031784/ , and the model form proposed is given in equation 2 of the paper.

Thanks to Rue or others who might be able to help.

James
